- When sentiment is consistently negative or near-zero, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high.
- If sentiment turns negative mid-period, model frequently fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias proportional to sentiment magnitude (e.g., -0.1×sentiment for 1–2% price drop).
- Model underestimates prices when sentiment is weak or neutral; increase forecast by 1–3% if sentiment < 0.30 over last 5 days.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag: model often misses early correction or mean-reversion; adjust by adding 1–2 days of lagged sentiment smoothing to forecast curve.
- When sentiment history shows repeated negative swings, model tends to overcorrect; apply dampening factor (e.g., 0.85×forecast) to avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment shifts.
